ch1.q: In a data set about 10 tablets with columns Tablet name, Cost, OS, Display Size and Battery Life, how many variables are there?
ch1.e: 變數是元素的特徵（欄）。Tablet name 只是用來辨認元素的名稱，不算變數，所以是 Cost、OS、Display Size、Battery Life 共 4 個。

ch1.q: Temperature measured in degrees Celsius is measured on which scale?
ch1.e: 0°C 不代表「沒有溫度」，沒有真正的 0，20°C 也不是 10°C 的兩倍熱，所以是區間尺度（interval）。

ch1.q: Students are coded 1 = Management, 2 = Engineering, 3 = Medicine. This variable is:
ch1.e: 數字只是代碼，沒有大小順序，加減平均沒意義 → 類別資料、名目尺度。類別資料可以是數字。

ch1.q: Which scale has a true zero, so that ratios of values are meaningful?
ch1.e: 比率尺度（ratio）有真正的 0，例如價格 200 元是 100 元的兩倍。

ch1.q: The number of building permits issued in Taipei in each of the last 36 months is an example of:
ch1.e: 同一個對象（台北市）、多個時間點 → 時間序列。同一時間、多個對象才是橫斷面。

ch1.q: A study compares lung health of smokers and nonsmokers without assigning who smokes. This is:
ch1.e: 研究者沒有控制誰抽菸，只是觀察 → 觀察研究（observational study）。

ch1.q: Using data from a sample to estimate a characteristic of the population is called:
ch1.e: 用樣本推論母體＝統計推論（statistical inference）。只摘要手上資料是敘述統計。

ch1.q: A data set has 25 elements and 6 variables. How many data values does it contain?
ch1.e: 資料值總數＝元素數 × 變數數 = 25 × 6 = 150。

ch1.q: Customers rate satisfaction from 1 = very dissatisfied to 5 = very satisfied, and a report states the average rating is 3.7. Which statement is most accurate?
o: The data are ratio, so the mean is fully meaningful
The data are ordinal; the mean assumes equal gaps between ratings, so the median or mode is safer
The data are nominal because the ratings are codes
The data are interval because they are numbers
ch1.e: 滿意度有順序但間距不一定相等 → 順序尺度（ordinal）。平均數假設「1 到 2」和「4 到 5」距離一樣，嚴格來說不適合，用中位數或眾數比較安全。是數字不代表就是區間或比率。

ch1.q: Which variable is measured on an interval scale rather than a ratio scale?
ch1.e: 西元年份的 0 年不代表「沒有時間」，2004 年也不是 1002 年的兩倍 → 區間尺度。工作年資 0 年＝完全沒有經驗，是比率尺度。

ch1.q: A data set records the ZIP code, age and GPA of 200 students. How many of these variables are quantitative?
ch1.e: 郵遞區號雖然是數字，但加減平均沒有意義，是類別資料。數量變數只有年齡和 GPA，共 2 個。

ch1.q: A company records the daily sales of 30 stores for 12 months. Which description is correct?
o: Both: each day across the 30 stores is cross-sectional, and each store over time is a time series
ch1.e: 固定某一天看 30 家店＝橫斷面；固定某一家店看 12 個月＝時間序列。這種同時有兩個面向的資料兩者都包含。

ch1.q: Researchers randomly assign 100 volunteers to take a drug or a placebo and compare blood pressure. Which pair is correct?
o: Observational study; only descriptive statistics are needed
Experimental study; conclusions about all patients require statistical inference
Observational study; cause and effect is proven
ch1.e: 研究者控制誰吃藥 → 實驗研究。100 人只是樣本，要推論到所有病人就需要統計推論。

ch1.q: In a data set, what is an element?
o: The measurement scale of a variable
The entity on which data are collected (one row of the table)
A characteristic of interest (one column of the table)
The total number of data values
ch1.e: Element＝被蒐集資料的對象，是表格的列；variable 才是欄。

ch1.q: The set of measurements obtained for one particular element is called:
ch1.e: Observation＝某一元素在所有變數上的量測結果，就是一整列。n 個元素 → n 個觀測值。

ch1.q: Product quality rated as poor, average, good or excellent is measured on which scale?
ch1.e: 有順序的標籤，但間距沒有意義 → 順序尺度（ordinal）。

ch1.q: Which statement about categorical data is correct?
o: Categorical data are measured on an interval or ratio scale
Categorical data must always be recorded as text
Categorical data allow more statistical methods than quantitative data
Arithmetic operations such as averaging are not meaningful, even when the categories are coded with numbers
ch1.e: 類別資料用名目或順序尺度；就算用數字代碼（1=管理、2=工程），平均也沒有意義，可用的分析方法比較少。

ch1.q: The number of building permits issued in each county of Taiwan in September 2025 is an example of:
ch1.e: 同一時間點、多個對象 → 橫斷面資料；同一對象、多個時間點才是時間序列。

ch1.q: Collecting data from every element of the population is called:
ch1.e: 調查整個母體＝普查（census）；只調查一部分＝抽樣調查（sample survey）。

ch1.q: Using historical data to build a model that forecasts next month's demand is an example of:
ch1.e: 描述性：過去發生什麼；預測性：用過去資料建模預測未來；處方性：給出最佳行動方案。

ch2.q: A frequency distribution has a class with frequency 8 out of n = 40. What is its percent frequency?
Which graph is used for categorical data and has bars separated by gaps?
ch2.e: 長條圖（bar chart）用於類別資料，長條分開；直方圖（histogram）用於數量資料，長條相連。

ch2.q: A histogram has a long tail on the right. The distribution is:
ch2.e: 偏態方向看尾巴：長尾在右＝右偏（正偏），平均數被大值拉高，通常 mean > median。

ch2.q: In a stretched stem-and-leaf display, where does the value 47 go?
ch2.e: 伸展莖葉圖每個莖寫兩次，第一行放葉 0～4，第二行放葉 5～9。47 的葉是 7 → 第二個 4。

ch2.q: Data range from 52 to 109 and you want 6 classes. The approximate class width is:
What does a cumulative frequency distribution show?
o: The number of items in each class only
The number of items less than or equal to the upper limit of each class
The percentage of items above each class
ch2.e: 累積次數＝到該組上限為止共有幾個（≤ upper limit）。最後一組的累積次數一定等於 n。

ch2.q: Conclusions from an aggregated crosstabulation reverse when the data are split into groups. This is called:
ch2.e: 辛普森悖論：合併資料與分組資料的結論相反，通常因為隱藏變數或各組樣本數差很多。

ch2.q: Which display shows the relationship between two quantitative variables?
ch2.e: 散佈圖（scatter diagram）＋趨勢線：兩個數量變數之間的關係。

ch2.q: A frequency distribution has classes 10–19: 4, 20–29: 9, 30–39: 7 (n = 20). What is the cumulative relative frequency for values ≤ 29?
ch2.e: 累積次數 ≤ 29 = 4 + 9 = 13，累積相對次數 = 13/20 = .65。.45 只是 20–29 這一組自己的相對次數。

ch2.q: A sector of a pie chart measures 72°. What percentage of the data does that class represent?
Alan completes 9 of 10 tasks in Project 1 and 50 of 100 in Project 2. John completes 80 of 100 in Project 1 and 4 of 10 in Project 2. Which conclusion is correct?
o: Alan is better in both projects and overall
John is better in both projects and overall
Alan has the higher completion rate in each project, but John is higher overall
ch2.e: 分開看：Alan 90% > 80%、50% > 40%。合併：Alan 59/110 = 53.6%，John 84/110 = 76.4%。結論反轉，這就是辛普森悖論，原因是兩人在各專案的工作量差很多。

ch2.q: Values such as 8.6, 9.4 and 11.7 are shown in a stem-and-leaf display with leaf unit 0.1. How is 11.7 displayed?
ch2.e: 葉單位 0.1 → 葉代表小數第一位。11.7 的莖是 11、葉是 7。

ch2.q: A histogram of 50 values is drawn with only 2 very wide classes. What is the main problem?
o: The shape of the distribution is hidden because the data are over-summarized
The histogram becomes a bar chart
The total frequency will not be 50
ch2.e: 組數太少，資料被壓縮成兩根長條，看不出偏態或集中位置。課本建議通常用 5～20 組。

ch2.q: Hotel A has 10 Excellent ratings out of 20 reviews; Hotel B has 50 Excellent ratings out of 200. Which comparison is correct?
o: Hotel B is better because it has more Excellent ratings
They cannot be compared because the sample sizes differ
Hotel A has the higher relative frequency of Excellent (50% vs 25%)

ch2.q: A class has relative frequency 0.25. What angle does it get in a pie chart?
How many classes does a frequency distribution for quantitative data usually have?
o: As many classes as data values
ch2.e: 通常 5～20 組：太少會把形狀蓋掉，太多又看不出規律。

ch2.q: How does a histogram differ from a bar chart?
o: A histogram is for quantitative data and its bars touch; a bar chart is for categorical data with gaps between bars
A histogram is for categorical data; a bar chart is for quantitative data
ch2.e: 直方圖：數量資料、長條相連；長條圖：類別資料、長條之間分開。

ch2.q: With a leaf unit of 10, how is the value 1682 shown in a stem-and-leaf display?
ch2.e: 葉單位 10：1682 → 莖 16、葉 8（捨去個位數，不是四捨五入成 9）。

ch2.q: Scores on a very easy exam have a long tail on the left. Which is most likely?
ch2.e: 左偏（長尾在左）：偏態係數 < 0，平均數被尾巴往左拉，通常平均數 < 中位數。

ch2.q: In a stacked bar chart drawn with percentages, the bars:
o: Must be separated into side-by-side bars
Have heights equal to the group totals
Can only show one category each
ch2.e: 用百分比畫的堆疊長條圖，每根長條都堆到 100%，只比較組成比例。

ch3.q: Returns over three years are +20%, −10%, +10%. What is the geometric mean annual return?
Using L = (p/100)(n + 1), what is the location of the 25th percentile when n = 21?
Why does the sample variance divide by n − 1 instead of n?
o: To make the variance larger than the standard deviation
Because deviations from x̄ tend to be smaller than deviations from μ, so dividing by n would underestimate σ²
Because one value is always an outlier
It is only a convention with no reason
ch3.e: 貝塞爾修正：樣本資料離 x̄ 比離真正的 μ 近，用 n 會低估母體變異數，所以除以 n − 1。

ch3.q: Data set A: mean 100, s = 10. Data set B: mean 1000, s = 50. Which has more relative variability?
ch3.e: 變異係數 CV = s / x̄ × 100%。A = 10%、B = 5%，A 的相對變異較大，雖然 B 的標準差較大。

ch3.q: The distribution is unknown. At least what percent of values lie within 2 standard deviations of the mean?
ch3.e: 分布未知 → 用柴比雪夫：1 − 1/2² = 75%。95% 是經驗法則，只適用鐘形分布。

ch3.q: Mean = 40, s = 5. What is the z-score of 50?
ch3.e: z = (50 − 40)/5 = 2，代表比平均高 2 個標準差。

ch3.q: Q1 = 545 and Q3 = 625. What is the upper limit for detecting outliers on a box plot?
A correlation coefficient of −0.96 indicates:
o: That X causes Y to decrease
ch3.e: r 接近 −1 → 強烈負線性關係。相關不等於因果，所以不能說 X 造成 Y。

ch3.q: Five values have a mean of 10. A sixth value, 22, is added. What is the new mean?
ch3.e: 原本總和 = 5 × 10 = 50，加入 22 後總和 72，新平均 = 72 / 6 = 12。不能直接把 10 和 22 平均成 16。

ch3.q: Adding 10 to every value in a data set changes which measures?
o: The mean and median only; the range, variance and standard deviation stay the same
The mean, median and standard deviation
ch3.e: 每個值都加 10，整組資料只是平移：位置量數（平均數、中位數）都加 10，離散量數（全距、變異數、標準差）不變。

ch3.q: For the sample 2, 4, 6, 8, what is the sample variance?
By Chebyshev's theorem, at least what percentage of values lie within 1.5 standard deviations of the mean?
Household income is skewed to the right and the mean is $62,000. The median is most likely:
ch3.e: 右偏時少數高所得把平均數往上拉，所以平均數 > 中位數，中位數會低於 62,000。

ch3.q: The sample covariance of X (in meters) and Y is 4. If X is converted to centimeters, what happens?
o: The covariance becomes 400 and the correlation is unchanged
The covariance becomes 400 and the correlation becomes 100 times larger
The covariance becomes 0.04 and the correlation is unchanged
ch3.e: 共變異數受單位影響：X 乘 100，共變異數也乘 100。相關係數沒有單位，永遠在 −1 到 +1，不會改變。

ch3.q: A student earns A (4 points) in a 3-credit course, B (3 points) in a 4-credit course and C (2 points) in a 1-credit course. What is the GPA?
What is the median of 3, 8, 5, 10, 7, 12?
o: 7.5 is not possible because n is even

ch3.q: Using L = (p/100)(n + 1), what is Q3 of the sorted data 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10, 11, 13, 15?
Which measure of variability is NOT affected by extreme values?
ch3.e: IQR = Q3 − Q1，只看中間 50% 的資料，不受極端值影響；全距對極端值最敏感。

ch3.q: A bell-shaped distribution has mean 40 and standard deviation 5. Approximately what percentage of the values lie between 30 and 50?
ch3.e: 30～50 是 μ ± 2σ；鐘形分布用經驗法則 → 約 95%。（分布未知才用柴比雪夫的「至少 75%」。）

ch3.q: Numerical measures such as μ and σ computed from the whole population are called:
ch3.e: 由母體算出的是參數（parameter，μ、σ）；由樣本算出的是統計量（statistic，x̄、s），可當參數的點估計量。

ch4.q: How many ways can a team leader and an assistant leader be chosen from 5 people?
ch4.e: 順序重要（隊長≠副隊長）→ 排列 P(5,2) = 5!/3! = 20。若順序不重要是組合 C(5,2) = 10。

ch4.q: Assigning probabilities using historical data, such as 18 of 40 days, is the:
ch4.e: 用實驗或歷史資料算比例＝相對次數法。等可能＝古典法；專家判斷＝主觀法。

ch4.q: Two events with nonzero probabilities are mutually exclusive. Then they are:
ch4.e: 互斥時一個發生，另一個機率變 0，機率改變了 → 一定不獨立。

ch4.q: In a crosstab of 800 homes, 100 are priced below $150,000 and 10 of those took over 90 days. P(over 90 days | below $150,000) is:
ch4.e: 條件機率的分母縮小到條件那一群：10/100 = 0.10。

ch4.q: Events A and B are independent if:
ch4.e: 獨立：P(A | B) = P(A)，等價於 P(A ∩ B) = P(A)P(B)。P(A ∩ B) = 0 是互斥。

ch4.q: In the Bayes tabular method, column 4 (prior × conditional) gives:
ch4.e: 第 (4) 欄是聯合機率 P(Aᵢ ∩ B) = P(Aᵢ)P(B | Aᵢ)，加總得 P(B)；第 (5) 欄才是事後機率。

ch4.q: A test has a false-positive rate of 0.75. This means:
ch4.e: 偽陽性＝沒病卻驗出陽性，所以是 P(+ | 沒病) = 0.75。P(有病 | 陽性) 要用貝氏定理算。

ch4.q: P(A) = 0.3 and P(B) = 0.4, and A and B are independent. What is P(A ∪ B)?
P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.4 and P(A ∪ B) = 0.7. Are A and B independent?
ch4.e: 先用加法律反推：P(A ∩ B) = 0.5 + 0.4 − 0.7 = 0.2。P(A)P(B) = 0.2，相等 → 獨立。有交集不代表不獨立。

ch4.q: Three of 10 applicants will be hired for three identical positions. How many different groups are possible?
ch4.e: 職位相同 → 順序不重要 → 組合 C(10,3) = 120。720 是排列，用在三個不同職位。

ch4.q: A disease affects 1% of people. A test is correct 99% of the time for both sick and healthy people. Given a positive result, the probability of being sick is closest to:
P(A) = 0.6 and P(B) = 0.5. Which of the following is impossible?
o: A and B are mutually exclusive
ch4.e: 若互斥，P(A ∪ B) = 0.6 + 0.5 = 1.1 > 1，不可能。其他三個選項在 A、B 獨立時都成立。

ch4.q: In a Bayes table, the conditional probabilities P(B | Aᵢ) in column (3) add up to 1.1. What does this mean?
o: There must be a calculation error
Nothing is wrong: P(B | A₁) and P(B | A₂) are conditioned on different events, so they need not add to 1
The posterior probabilities will add up to 1.1
ch4.e: 第 (3) 欄的條件不同（一個在 A₁ 之下、一個在 A₂ 之下），加總沒有必須等於 1 的道理。必須等於 1 的是第 (2) 欄事前機率和第 (5) 欄事後機率。

ch4.q: An experiment has two steps: the first has 4 possible outcomes and the second has 2. How many experimental outcomes are there?
ch4.e: 多步驟計數法則：4 × 2 = 8（Bradley：Markley Oil 4 種 × Collins Mining 2 種）。

ch4.q: How many different 2-person teams can be formed from 5 people (order does not matter)?
Assigning probability 1/6 to each face of a fair die uses the:
ch4.e: 各結果等可能、每個 1/n → 古典法（classical method）。

ch4.q: P(A) = 0.35. What is P(Aᶜ)?
Prior probabilities P(A₁) = 0.7 and P(A₂) = 0.3; P(B | A₁) = 0.2 and P(B | A₂) = 0.9. What is P(A₁ | B)?
In a joint probability table, P(A ∩ B) = 0.12 and P(B) = 0.40. What is P(A | B)?

ch1.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the three main components of the CPU?
ch1.e: CPU = CU + ALU + Registers（控制、運算、暫存）。DMA controller（直接記憶體存取控制器）在 I/O device 那一側，不在 CPU 裡。

ch1.q: What is the main benefit of DMA (direct memory access)?
o: Main memory keeps its data when power is lost
The device controller transfers a whole block directly to main memory without CPU intervention, generating only one interrupt per block
User mode can execute privileged instructions
ch1.e: 關鍵字：high-speed I/O、directly to main memory、without CPU intervention、one interrupt per block（每個 block 只產生一次 interrupt）。

ch1.q: What is a trap (exception)?
o: A hardware interrupt generated by the timer
A software-generated interrupt caused by an error or a user request
A notification that a DMA transfer has finished
ch1.e: Trap = software-generated interrupt（軟體產生的中斷），例如 division by zero（除以 0）或 system call（系統呼叫）。

ch1.q: Where is the bootstrap program typically stored?
ch1.e: Bootstrap program（開機程式）存在 ROM／EPROM，稱為 firmware（韌體）；它初始化系統並把 kernel（核心）載入 memory。

ch1.q: What is the only large storage medium that the CPU can access directly?
ch1.e: Main memory（主記憶體）：CPU 唯一能直接存取的大型儲存，random access（隨機存取），通常 volatile（斷電資料消失）。

ch1.q: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of multiprocessor systems?
ch1.e: 三大優點：increased throughput（吞吐量）、economy of scale（規模經濟）、increased reliability（可靠度，graceful degradation／fault tolerance）。跟 deadlock 無關。

ch1.q: What is the main difference between timesharing and multiprogramming?
o: Timesharing can run only one program
In timesharing the CPU switches jobs so frequently that users can interact with each job (response time < 1 second)
ch1.e: Multiprogramming（多元程式）讓 CPU 不閒著，目的是 efficiency（效率）；timesharing（分時）切換快到 user 可以 interact（互動）。

ch1.q: What is the mode bit used for?
o: Distinguishing whether the system is running user code or kernel code
ch1.e: Dual-mode operation（雙模式）：user mode（使用者模式）／kernel mode（核心模式），用 hardware 提供的 mode bit 區分。Privileged instructions（特權指令）只能在 kernel mode 執行。

ch1.q: What is the purpose of a timer?
o: To display the correct clock time
To prevent an infinite loop or a process hogging resources by generating an interrupt after a specific period
ch1.e: Timer（計時器）時間到就產生 interrupt，讓 OS 拿回 CPU 的控制權。

ch1.q: Which statement about programs and processes is correct?
o: A program is an active entity
A process is an executable file stored on disk
A process is a program in execution and is an active entity
One program can become only one process
ch1.e: Program（程式）是 passive entity（被動）；process（行程）是 active entity（主動）。一個 program 可以變成多個 process。

ch1.q: Moving up the storage hierarchy (toward registers and cache), storage becomes:
ch1.e: Storage hierarchy（儲存階層）依 speed、cost、volatility 排列：越上層越快、越貴、容量越小。

ch1.q: A device controller moves a 4 KB block to main memory using DMA. How many interrupts does the CPU receive for this block?
ch1.e: DMA 的重點：one interrupt per block（每個 block 一次）。如果是一般 interrupt-driven I/O，才會每個 byte 中斷一次（4096 次）。

ch1.q: If the hardware had NO timer, which problem could the OS NOT stop?
o: A division by zero in a user program
A user program that enters an infinite loop and never calls the OS
A user program that tries to execute a privileged instruction
A user program that requests I/O
ch1.e: 除以零、執行特權指令都會產生 trap，OS 自然拿回控制權；要 I/O 會呼叫 system call。只有無窮迴圈不會主動交還控制權，必須靠 timer interrupt（計時器中斷）。

ch1.q: A system keeps several jobs in memory and switches jobs ONLY when the running job waits for I/O. Users complain that the response time is several seconds. Which description fits?
ch1.e: 只在等 I/O 時才切換 = multiprogramming（目標是效率）。Timesharing 會頻繁切換，讓回應時間 < 1 秒（目標是互動）。

ch1.q: A server with 10 CPUs keeps running at a lower speed after one CPU fails. This property is called:
ch1.e: Graceful degradation（降級運作）：壞一部分，還能用但變慢。Fault tolerance（容錯）更強：壞一部分也像沒事一樣繼續。兩個很容易搞混。

ch1.q: Which statement is FALSE?
o: A trap is a software-generated interrupt
A system call switches the mode bit to kernel mode
A system call is a hardware interrupt sent by the device controller
The interrupt architecture must save the address of the interrupted instruction
ch1.e: System call 是程式自己發出的 trap（軟體中斷），不是裝置控制器送來的硬體中斷。

ch1.q: Which program is described as "the one program running at all times on the computer"?
ch1.e: Kernel（核心）＝一直在執行的那一個程式；其他東西不是 system program 就是 application program。Bootstrap program 只在開機時執行。

ch1.q: The CPU looks for a piece of data in the cache and does not find it. What happens next?
o: The data is copied from the slower storage into the cache, then used from the cache
The CPU waits for a timer interrupt
The data is used directly from the disk and never copied
The whole cache is cleared and the program restarts
ch1.e: Caching：先查 cache；有就直接用，沒有就先把資料從較慢的那一層複製進 cache，再從 cache 使用。

ch1.q: In a multiprocessor system where every CPU has its own cache, what must the hardware provide so that all caches hold the most recent value of a variable?
ch1.e: Multiprocessor 環境每顆 CPU 都有自己的 cache，硬體必須提供 cache coherency（快取一致性），讓每顆 CPU 的 cache 都是最新值。

ch1.q: Which statement describes asymmetric clustering?
o: One machine stays in hot-standby mode and takes over only if another fails
All nodes run applications and monitor each other
Several cores on one chip share the same memory
Each processor performs all tasks; no processor is the boss
ch1.e: Asymmetric clustering：一台 hot-standby 待命，別台壞了才接手。Symmetric clustering：多個節點都在跑應用程式並互相監控。最後一個選項描述的是 SMP。

ch2.q: What does it mean when a process is in the ready state?
o: It is waiting for an I/O operation to complete
It is waiting to be assigned to a processor
ch2.e: Ready（就緒）：等 CPU。等 I/O 是 waiting（等待）。

ch2.q: When the I/O of a waiting process completes, which state does it enter?
ch2.e: I/O or event completion → ready（重新排隊），不是直接回 running。

ch2.q: In the process state diagram, what is the transition from running to ready called?
ch2.e: running → ready 是 interrupt（中斷）；ready → running 才是 scheduler dispatch（排程器派送）。

ch2.q: In which section of a process's memory are local variables stored?
ch2.e: Stack（堆疊）：function parameters、return address、local variables。Global variables 在 data section。

ch2.q: Memory allocated by malloc() at run time is in the:
ch2.e: Heap（堆積）= memory dynamically allocated during run time（執行時動態配置）。

ch2.q: Which of the following is NOT stored in a PCB?
o: The source code of other processes
ch2.e: PCB（Process Control Block，行程控制區塊）：process state、program counter、CPU registers、CPU-scheduling info、memory-management info、accounting info、I/O status info。

ch2.q: Which scheduler decreases the degree of multiprogramming by swapping processes out to disk?
ch2.e: Mid-term scheduler（中期排程器）：swap out／swap in（換出／換入），降低 degree of multiprogramming（多元程式程度）。Long-term scheduler 控制它。

ch2.q: Which statement about the short-term scheduler is correct?
o: It is invoked only every few minutes
It is invoked very frequently (milliseconds), so it must be fast
It selects which processes enter the ready queue
ch2.e: Short-term scheduler（短期排程器，CPU scheduler）毫秒級頻繁執行，所以必須快。

ch2.q: What are the two models of interprocess communication (IPC)?
ch2.e: Two models of IPC（Interprocess Communication，行程間通訊）：shared memory（共享記憶體）與 message passing（訊息傳遞）。

ch2.q: With BUFFER_SIZE = 10, how many items can the in/out bounded-buffer solution hold at most?
ch2.e: Bounded buffer（有限緩衝區）最多 BUFFER_SIZE − 1 個。Full：(in+1) % SIZE == out；empty：in == out。

ch2.q: In message passing, when both send and receive are blocking, it is called a:
ch2.e: Both blocking → rendezvous（會合）。Blocking 也叫 synchronous（同步）。

ch2.q: What does the UNIX fork() system call do?
o: Replaces the process's memory space with a new program
Creates a new child process that is a duplicate of the parent
Sends a message to another process
ch2.e: fork() 建立 child process（子行程）；exec() 在 fork 之後用新 program 取代 memory space。

ch2.q: Which process-state transition is NOT possible?
ch2.e: 等完 I/O 的 process 要先回到 ready queue 排隊，再由 scheduler 挑中才能 running。不能從 waiting 直接跳到 running。

ch2.q: A bounded buffer uses in/out pointers with BUFFER_SIZE = 8. At most how many items can it hold at the same time?
ch2.e: 要永遠留一格空的，才能分辨 full（(in+1)%8 == out）和 empty（in == out），所以最多 BUFFER_SIZE − 1 = 7 個。

ch2.q: Which of the following does NOT happen during a context switch?
o: The old process's registers are saved into its PCB
The new process's saved state is loaded from its PCB
The new process's program code is reloaded from disk
The CPU does no useful work while switching
ch2.e: Context switch 只存／載入狀態（PCB 裡的 registers、PC 等），程式本身已經在記憶體裡，不會重新從硬碟載入。

ch2.q: After the shared region is set up, why is shared memory usually faster than message passing?
o: Reads and writes do not need system calls into the kernel
The kernel copies data in larger blocks
ch2.e: Shared memory 只有建立時需要 kernel；之後直接讀寫記憶體。Message passing 每次 send()/receive() 都要經過 kernel，所以比較慢。注意它仍然需要同步（synchronization）。

ch2.q: Which queue holds the processes that reside in main memory and are ready and waiting to execute?
ch2.e: Job queue＝系統中所有 process；Ready queue＝在主記憶體、準備好等著執行；Device queue＝在等某個 I/O 裝置。

ch2.q: A process that spends most of its time doing computation and has a few very long CPU bursts is called:
ch2.e: CPU-bound：大多時間在計算，少數很長的 CPU burst。I/O-bound：大多時間在做 I/O，很多短的 CPU burst。Long-term scheduler 要挑兩者的好組合（good process mix）。

ch2.q: Which is a property of indirect communication (mailboxes)?
o: A link may be associated with many processes, and a pair of processes may share several links
Each process must explicitly name the other process in send and receive
Exactly one link exists between each pair of processes
Messages never pass through the kernel
ch2.e: Indirect communication 透過 mailbox（port）：一條 link 可以連很多 process，每對 process 可以有多條 link。要指名對方、每對恰好一條 link 是 direct communication。

ch2.q: With a zero-capacity message queue, what must the sender do?
o: Wait until the receiver receives the message (rendezvous)
Wait only when n messages are already in the queue
Keep resending until the message is acknowledged
ch2.e: Zero capacity：sender 一定要等 receiver（rendezvous）。Bounded capacity：最多 n 個，滿了才等。Unbounded capacity：sender 永遠不用等。

ch3.q: Under which two circumstances is CPU scheduling nonpreemptive?
ch3.e: Process 自己放棄 CPU（去等 I/O 或結束）= nonpreemptive（不可搶奪）；其他都是 preemptive（可搶奪）。

ch3.q: "Short processes wait behind a long process" is called ___, and it occurs in ___.
ch3.e: Convoy effect（護航效應）：short process behind long process → FCFS（First-Come, First-Served，先到先服務）。

ch3.q: Which algorithm gives the minimum average waiting time (it is optimal)?
ch3.e: SJF（Shortest-Job-First，最短工作優先）is optimal；difficulty（困難）是無法得知下一次 CPU burst 的長度。

ch3.q: Which scheduling algorithms may suffer from starvation?
ch3.e: SJF（含 SRTF）一直挑短的，Priority 一直挑高 priority 的 → 長的或低 priority 的 process 可能永遠等（starvation 飢餓）。

ch3.q: What is the solution to starvation?
o: Aging: increase the priority of a process as it waits longer
ch3.e: Aging（老化）：as time progresses, increase the priority of the process。

ch3.q: If the time quantum in Round Robin is very large, RR becomes:
ch3.e: q large → FCFS；q small → context switch（內容切換）overhead 太高。

ch3.q: What is the main difference between multilevel queue and multilevel feedback queue scheduling?
o: Whether a process can move between queues
ch3.e: MLQ（Multilevel Queue，多層佇列）：process 永久在同一條 queue；MLFQ（Multilevel Feedback Queue，多層回饋佇列）：可以在 queues 之間移動（可實作 aging）。

ch3.q: How is waiting time computed?
o: Completion time − arrival time − burst time
ch3.e: Turnaround time（周轉時間）= completion − arrival；waiting time（等待時間）= turnaround − burst。

ch3.q: FCFS with P1 = 24, P2 = 3, P3 = 3 arriving at time 0 in the order P1, P2, P3. What is the average waiting time?
In rate-monotonic scheduling, how is priority assigned?
ch3.e: RMS（Rate-Monotonic Scheduling，速率單調排程）：priority = 1/period（固定）。看 deadline（截止期限）的是 EDF。

ch3.q: Exponential averaging with α = 1/2, τn = 10, tn = 6. What is τn+1?
What is dispatch latency?
o: Time from the arrival of an interrupt to the start of its service routine
Time for the dispatcher to stop one process and start another running
Time a process waits in the ready queue
The length of a CPU burst
ch3.e: Interrupt latency（中斷延遲）是中斷到開始處理；dispatch latency（派送延遲）是換 process 的時間。

ch3.q: P1, P2, P3, P4 all arrive at time 0 with CPU bursts 6, 8, 7, 3. What is the average waiting time under (nonpreemptive) SJF?
P1 = 24, P2 = 3, P3 = 3 (all arrive at 0, in that order). Round Robin with q = 4. What is the average waiting time?
SRTF (preemptive SJF): P1 arrives 0 burst 8, P2 arrives 1 burst 4, P3 arrives 2 burst 9, P4 arrives 3 burst 5. Average waiting time?
A process arrives at time 2, first gets the CPU at time 5, and finishes at time 12. Its CPU burst is 4. What is its waiting time?
ch3.e: Turnaround = 12 − 2 = 10；waiting = turnaround − burst = 10 − 4 = 6。3 是 response time（第一次拿到 CPU 的時間 − 到達時間），不是 waiting time。

ch3.q: Exponential averaging with α = 0.5: the last predicted burst τn = 10 and the actual burst tn = 6. What is the next prediction τn+1?
Which statement is TRUE?
o: RR always gives a lower average waiting time than FCFS
Preemptive priority scheduling cannot cause starvation
SJF gives the minimum average waiting time for a given set of processes
In a multilevel queue, processes move down when they use too much CPU
ch3.e: SJF 是 optimal（平均等待最小）。RR 的平均等待常常比 FCFS 長；preemptive priority 一樣會 starvation；會往下移動的是 multilevel FEEDBACK queue，不是 multilevel queue。

ch3.q: Which scheduling criterion should be MAXIMIZED?
ch3.e: 要最大：CPU utilization、throughput。要最小：turnaround time、waiting time、response time。口訣「前兩個要大，後三個要小」。

ch3.q: How does earliest-deadline-first (EDF) scheduling assign priorities?
o: Dynamically: the earlier the deadline, the higher the priority
Statically: the shorter the period, the higher the priority
By the predicted length of the next CPU burst
By the number of shares each process owns
ch3.e: EDF：依 deadline 動態決定，deadline 越早越優先。依 period 給固定優先權的是 RMS；依 shares 分配的是 proportional share scheduling。

ch4.q: What are the two types of parallelism?
ch4.e: Data parallelism（資料平行）：同一種操作做在不同的資料子集；task parallelism（工作平行）：不同 thread 做不同的事。

ch4.q: An application is 75% parallel and 25% serial. By Amdahl's law, what is the speedup from 1 core to 2 cores?
By Amdahl's law, as the number of cores N approaches infinity, the speedup approaches:
o: 1/S, where S is the serial portion
ch4.e: Serial portion（序列部分）決定上限：speedup → 1/S。

ch4.q: What is a disadvantage of the many-to-one model?
o: It creates too many kernel threads
One blocking thread blocks all threads, and threads cannot run in parallel on multicore systems
ch4.e: Many-to-one（多對一）：one thread blocking causes all to block；一次只有一個 thread 能進 kernel。

ch4.q: What is the two-level model?
o: Many-to-many, but also allows a user thread to be bound to a kernel thread
A process with exactly two threads
ch4.e: Two-level model（兩層模型）：similar to M:M, except that it allows a user thread to be bound（綁定）to a kernel thread。

ch4.q: Which multithreading model do Linux and Windows use?
ch4.e: One-to-one（一對一）：Windows、Linux、Solaris 9 and later。

ch4.q: Which of the following does each thread of the same process have on its own?
ch4.e: Threads（執行緒）共享 code、data、files；各自有 registers（暫存器）、stack、program counter。

ch4.q: Which statement about concurrency and parallelism is correct?
o: A single-core system can provide concurrency but not true parallelism
A single-core system can provide parallelism
They mean exactly the same thing
Parallelism does not require multiple cores
ch4.e: Concurrency（並行）：多個 task 都有進度，可以輪流；parallelism（平行）：真的同時執行，需要 multiple cores。

ch4.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the four benefits of multithreading?
ch4.e: 四個 benefits：responsiveness（回應性）、resource sharing（資源共享）、economy（經濟）、scalability（可擴展性）。

ch4.q: What is Pthreads?
o: A POSIX standard API for thread creation and synchronization: a specification, not an implementation
ch4.e: Pthreads：POSIX standard（IEEE 1003.1c），只規定行為（specification 規格），實作由 library 決定。

ch4.q: Which of the following is NOT a method of implicit threading?
ch4.e: Implicit threading（隱式執行緒）三種：thread pools（執行緒池）、OpenMP、GCD。fork() 是建立 process 的 system call。

ch4.q: An application is 75% parallel and 25% serial. By Amdahl's law, what is the speedup on 4 cores?
For the same application (25% serial), what is the maximum speedup no matter how many cores are added?
ch4.e: N → ∞ 時 speedup → 1/S = 1/0.25 = 4。循序部分決定上限。

ch4.q: A process uses the many-to-one model with 8 user threads on a 4-core machine. At most how many of its threads can run at the same instant?
ch4.e: Many-to-one 只有一個 kernel thread，一次只有一個 thread 能進 kernel，所以多核心也只能跑 1 個。

ch4.q: Two threads read the SAME array: one finds the minimum, the other finds the maximum. This is an example of:
ch4.e: 關鍵在「做的事不一樣」（找最小 vs 找最大）→ task parallelism。如果是把陣列切兩半、兩個 thread 都做加總，才是 data parallelism。

ch4.q: Which of the following is NOT shared by the threads of the same process?
ch4.e: 每個 thread 有自己的 stack、registers 和 PC（thread ID 也是自己的）；code、data（全域變數）、open files 是共用的。

ch4.q: Which statement is TRUE?
o: Concurrency is impossible on a single-core CPU
Parallelism is possible on a single-core CPU
It is possible to have concurrency without parallelism
Parallelism and concurrency mean the same thing
ch4.e: 單核心輪流執行就有 concurrency（每個工作都有進展），但沒有 parallelism（真正同時）。平行需要多核心。

ch4.q: Which is an advantage of using a thread pool?
o: Servicing a request with an existing thread is usually faster than creating a new thread
Every request gets its own brand-new kernel thread
It removes the need for any thread library
It lets a single-core CPU run threads truly in parallel
ch4.e: Thread pool 的好處：(1) 用現成的 thread 比新建快；(2) thread 數量被 pool 大小限制；(3) 把要做的工作和建立工作的機制分開。

ch4.q: In OpenMP, what does #pragma omp parallel do?
o: Creates as many threads as there are processing cores
Moves the block to a dispatch queue
Turns the block into a separate process
ch4.e: #pragma omp parallel 建立跟核心數一樣多的 thread 平行執行那一段；#pragma omp parallel for 讓 for 迴圈平行。Dispatch queue 是 Grand Central Dispatch 的東西。

ch4.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the challenges of multicore programming?
ch4.e: 五個挑戰：dividing activities、balance、data splitting、data dependency、testing and debugging。Time quantum 是 Round Robin 排班的參數。

ch5.q: Which of the following is NOT a necessary condition for deadlock?
ch5.e: 四個 necessary conditions（必要條件）：mutual exclusion（互斥）、hold and wait（持有並等待）、no preemption（不可搶奪）、circular wait（循環等待）。

ch5.q: A resource-allocation graph contains a cycle, and each resource type has only one instance. Then:
o: The system is in a safe state
ch5.e: Single instance（單一實例）+ cycle（環）→ deadlock。

ch5.q: A resource-allocation graph contains a cycle, and resource types have several instances. Then:
o: There is a possibility of deadlock
ch5.e: Several instances（多個實例）+ cycle → possibility of deadlock（可能死結）。

ch5.q: What is the relationship between safe states and deadlock?
o: Safe state → no deadlock; unsafe state → possibility of deadlock
ch5.e: Deadlock ⊂ unsafe state（不安全狀態）。Avoidance（避免）就是確保系統永遠不進入 unsafe state。

ch5.q: In the banker's algorithm, how is Need computed?
ch5.e: Need[i,j] = Max[i,j] − Allocation[i,j]（還需要 = 最大需求 − 已分配）。

ch5.q: In the safety algorithm, when a process can finish, Work is increased by its:
ch5.e: 它做完會把手上持有的 Allocation（已分配資源）還回來：Work = Work + Allocation。最常錯！

ch5.q: Which algorithm is used for deadlock avoidance when resource types have multiple instances?
ch5.e: Single instance → resource-allocation graph（資源配置圖，claim edge 宣告邊）；multiple instances → banker's algorithm（銀行家演算法）。

ch5.q: Numbering all resource types and requiring requests in increasing order prevents which condition?
ch5.e: Impose a total ordering（全序）of all resource types → 不可能形成 circular wait（循環等待）。

ch5.q: In the resource-request algorithm, if Request > Available, then:
o: Raise an error because the process exceeded its maximum claim
ch5.e: Request > Need → error（超過宣告的最大需求）；Request > Available → must wait（必須等待）。

ch5.q: Which method detects deadlock when every resource type has a single instance?
ch5.e: Wait-for graph（等待圖）：只有 process 節點，定期找 cycle，需要 O(n²)。

ch5.q: How do most operating systems actually handle deadlocks?
o: They ignore the problem and pretend deadlocks never occur
ch5.e: Ignore the problem（忽略問題）and pretend that deadlocks never occur; used by most operating systems。

ch5.q: Work = (3,3,2). P1 has Need = (1,2,2) and Allocation = (2,0,0). After P1 finishes, Work = ?
A resource-allocation graph contains a cycle, and one resource type in the cycle has 2 instances. What can you conclude?
o: There may or may not be a deadlock
The system is in a safe state
ch5.e: 有環 + 多個 instance → 只是「可能」死結。只有在每種資源都只有一個 instance 時，有環才一定死結。

ch5.q: Total 12 tape drives. P0: Max 10, Allocation 5; P1: Max 4, Allocation 2; P2: Max 9, Allocation 2. If P2 requests 1 more drive, should it be granted?
o: No, the resulting state is unsafe
No, because P2's request exceeds its Max
ch5.e: 假裝給：Available = 3 − 1 = 2。P1 還要 2 → 做完 → Available 4。P0 還要 5、P2 還要 6，都 > 4，找不到安全順序 → unsafe，要等。只檢查 request ≤ Available 是陷阱。

ch5.q: Requiring every process to request and be allocated all its resources before it starts executing denies which condition?
ch5.e: 一開始就拿齊，執行中就不會「拿著一些、再等另一些」→ 破壞 hold and wait。破壞 circular wait 的方法是資源排序（total ordering）。

ch5.q: Which statement is TRUE?
o: Every unsafe state is a deadlock
Every deadlock state is an unsafe state
A safe state can still deadlock
Deadlock avoidance needs no advance information
ch5.e: Deadlock ⊂ unsafe：死結一定不安全，但不安全不一定死結。Safe state 一定不會死結；避免法需要事先知道每個 process 的 Max。

ch5.q: Available = (3,3,2). P1's Need = (1,2,2) and P1 requests (1,0,2). If the Banker's algorithm pretends to grant it, what is the new Available?
ch5.e: 先檢查 (1,0,2) ≤ Need (1,2,2) 且 ≤ Available (3,3,2)。假裝給：Available = (3,3,2) − (1,0,2) = (2,3,0)。之後還要跑 safety algorithm 確認安全才真的給。

ch5.q: How is a wait-for graph obtained from a resource-allocation graph?
o: Remove the resource nodes and draw Pi → Pj when Pi is waiting for a resource held by Pj
Remove the process nodes and keep only the resource nodes
Turn every claim edge into an assignment edge
Add a dashed edge for every future request
ch5.e: Wait-for graph：拿掉 resource 節點，「Pi 等的 resource 在 Pj 手上」就畫 Pi → Pj。每種 resource 只有一個 instance 時，有 cycle 就有 deadlock。

ch5.q: How does the deadlock-detection algorithm (several instances per resource type) differ from the Banker's safety algorithm?
o: It uses Request instead of Need, and a process with zero Allocation starts with Finish = true
It uses Max instead of Allocation
It only works when each resource type has one instance
It never adds anything to Work
ch5.e: Detection 跟 safety algorithm 幾乎一樣，差別：用 Request（目前的請求）取代 Need；Allocation 全為 0 的 process 一開始就 Finish = true；最後 Finish = false 的就是 deadlocked。

ch5.q: What is a drawback of preventing hold-and-wait by requiring each process to request all its resources before it starts?
o: Low resource utilization and possible starvation
All resource types must be numbered
Deadlocks can no longer be detected
ch5.e: 破壞 hold and wait 的缺點：resource 使用率低、可能 starvation。替 resource 編號、依遞增順序申請是破壞 circular wait 的做法。

ch1.q: Any algorithm could be written with only three programming constructs. Which are they?
ch1.e: 課本原文：sequence、selection、loop。

ch1.q: Which part of an algorithm header lists any precursor requirements for the parameters?
ch1.e: Precondition（前置條件）＝執行前參數要滿足什麼。

ch1.q: Which of the following is the best intelligent data name according to the textbook?
ch1.e: 單一字元與 generic name（count）都不好；numOfStu 是好縮寫，noStu 不是。

ch1.q: Which of the following is a composite data type?
ch1.e: 電話號碼 = area code + exchange + number，可以拆，所以是 composite。

ch1.q: Which statement best describes an Abstract Data Type?
o: A data type that can only store integers
A data declaration packaged together with the operations that are meaningful for the data type
A program written without any functions
A data structure stored contiguously in memory
ch1.e: ADT 的 formal definition。

ch1.q: What is the efficiency of the loop: for (i = 1; i <= n; i = i * 2)?
ch1.e: 控制變數每次乘 2 → logarithmic loop。

ch1.q: What is the Big-O of f(n) = 3n² + 5n log n + 100?
ch1.e: 係數設 1，只留最大項 n²。

ch1.q: Multiplying two n × n matrices with three nested loops has an efficiency of
ch1.e: 三層迴圈 → O(n³)；相加是兩層 → O(n²)。

ch1.q: Which ordering is correct from most efficient to least efficient?
o: O(log n) < O(n) < O(n log n) < O(n²) < O(2ⁿ)
O(n) < O(log n) < O(n²) < O(n log n) < O(2ⁿ)
O(log n) < O(n log n) < O(n) < O(n²) < O(n!)
O(1) < O(n) < O(log n) < O(n²) < O(n!)
ch1.e: log n < n < n log n < n² < nᵏ < cⁿ < n!

ch1.q: In the textbook’s pseudocode, arrays are indexed starting at
o: Any value chosen by the programmer
ch1.e: Pseudocode arrays are indexed starting at 0.

ch1.e: Encapsulation（封裝）是 OOP 的一部分。

ch1.q: Which of the following is an example of the government protecting property rights?

o: The government taxes high incomes at higher rates.
The central bank slows the growth of money.
The government gives food stamps to the poor.
Police stop people from stealing a farmer's crops.
oz: 政府對高所得者課較高稅率
中央銀行放慢貨幣成長
警察阻止別人偷農夫的作物
ch1.e: 保護財產權：沒人保護成果，就沒人敢投資和生產。課稅、發食物券是為了公平。

ch1.q: Market power refers to
ch1.qz: 市場力量指的是
o: the ability of a single economic actor (or small group) to have a substantial influence on market prices.
the total amount of goods produced in a market.
the ability of consumers to buy whatever they want.
the power of the government to set all prices.
oz: 單一經濟行為者（或一小群）大幅影響市場價格的能力
市場上生產的商品總量
消費者想買什麼就買什麼的能力
政府決定所有價格的權力
ch1.e: Market power：單一買方或賣方（例如壟斷）能影響價格，是市場失靈的原因之一。

ch1.q: Which of the following is an example of an externality?
ch1.qz: 下列哪一個是外部性的例子？
o: A firm raises its price because demand has increased.
Smoke from a factory harms the health of people living nearby.
A consumer buys a cheaper brand of coffee.
A worker quits a job to go back to school.
oz: 需求增加，廠商提高價格
工廠的廢氣傷害附近居民的健康
消費者改買比較便宜的咖啡
ch1.e: Externality：一個人的生產或消費影響到沒參與交易的旁人（污染、二手菸），俗稱「躺著也中槍」。

ch1.q: Giving food stamps to the poor and taxing high incomes at higher rates are policies mainly aimed at promoting
ch1.qz: 發食物券給窮人、對高所得者課較高稅率，主要是為了促進
ch1.e: 用稅和福利重分配所得 → 促進公平（equality）。修正外部性、市場力量才是為了效率。

ch1.q: Differences in living standards across countries are explained mainly by differences in
ch1.qz: 各國生活水準的差異，主要是由什麼差異造成的？
ch1.e: 原理 8：一國的生活水準取決於生產力（每單位勞動能生產多少），工會、外國競爭的影響小很多。

ch1.q: In the long run, a high rate of inflation is almost always caused by
ch1.qz: 長期來看，高通貨膨脹幾乎都是由什麼造成的？
o: rapid growth in the quantity of money.
ch1.e: 原理 9：政府印太多鈔票，物價就上漲；印得越快，通膨越高。

ch1.q: If the central bank slows the growth of money to reduce inflation, in the short run it will most likely cause
ch1.qz: 如果中央銀行放慢貨幣成長來壓低通膨，短期內最可能造成
o: no change in unemployment at all.
ch1.e: 原理 10：短期內通膨與失業有取捨，壓通膨 → 短期失業上升；長期兩者無關。

ch1.q: A firm has already spent $5 million on a project that cannot be recovered. Finishing it costs $1 million more, and the finished product can be sold for $3 million. The firm should
ch1.qz: 廠商已經在一個專案花了 500 萬（拿不回來）。再花 100 萬能完成，完成後可賣 300 萬。廠商應該
o: finish the project, because the future benefit of $3 million exceeds the future cost of $1 million.
finish only if it can be sold for more than $6 million.
stop, because the $5 million is already lost.
stop, because it will never earn back the $6 million in total.
oz: 完成，因為未來效益 300 萬大於未來成本 100 萬
只有能賣超過 600 萬才完成
停止，因為 500 萬已經虧掉了
停止，因為總共 600 萬永遠賺不回來
ch1.e: 500 萬是沉沒成本，跟決策無關。只比較未來：300 萬 > 100 萬 → 應該完成。

ch1.q: For the same project ($5 million already spent, product sells for $3 million), what is the most the firm should be willing to spend to finish it?
ch1.qz: 同一個專案（已花 500 萬，完成後可賣 300 萬），廠商最多願意再花多少錢完成它？
ch1.e: 沉沒成本不算，完成的效益是 300 萬，所以最多願意再付 300 萬。

ch1.q: You already spent $1,000 repairing an old car. Now the transmission needs a $900 repair. Repaired, the car sells for $6,300; unrepaired, it sells for $5,500. Should you repair it?
ch1.qz: 你已經花 1,000 修過舊車，現在變速箱要 900 修。修好可賣 6,300，不修可賣 5,500。該修嗎？
o: No, because the gain of $800 is less than the $900 cost.
Yes, because you already spent $1,000 on the car.
oz: 不修，因為好處 800 小於成本 900

ch1.q: Taoyuan's YouBike program gives the first 30 minutes free, and the city subsidy grew from NT$62 million to over NT$110 million. An economist would say the free rides
ch1.qz: 桃園 YouBike 前 30 分鐘免費，市府補貼從 6,200 萬增加到 1.1 億以上。經濟學家會說免費騎乘
o: have an opportunity cost: the subsidy could have been used for something else.
oz: 有機會成本：補貼的錢本來可以用在別的地方
ch1.e: 免費不代表沒成本，補貼的錢有機會成本（原理 2）；邊際成本 0 也讓人多騎（原理 3、4）。

ch1.q: An economist measures the profit of a firm as revenue minus
ch1.qz: 經濟學家衡量的利潤是收入減掉
ch1.e: 經濟利潤 = 收入 − 外顯 − 隱性成本；會計利潤只扣外顯成本，所以會計利潤 ≥ 經濟利潤。

ch1.q: Why is water, which is essential for life, cheaper than diamonds?
ch1.qz: 水是生活必需品，為什麼比鑽石便宜？
o: The marginal benefit of an extra cup of water is low because water is plentiful.
oz: 水很多，多一杯水的邊際利益很低
ch1.e: 價格反映邊際價值。水很多，多一單位的邊際利益小；鑽石稀少，多一顆的邊際利益大。

ch1.q: Bill Gates and Mark Zuckerberg left Harvard because they expected
ch1.qz: Bill Gates 和 Mark Zuckerberg 從哈佛休學，是因為他們預期
o: the benefit of school to exceed its cost.
the opportunity cost of staying in school to exceed its benefit.
oz: 留在學校的機會成本大於效益
ch1.e: 他們的時間太值錢（放棄的所得很高），上學的機會成本超過效益。

ch1.q: Which of the following is mainly about equality rather than efficiency?
ch1.qz: 下列哪一項主要是為了公平，而不是效率？
o: Higher income-tax rates on people with higher incomes.
oz: 高所得者適用較高所得稅率
ch1.e: 累進所得稅是重分配（公平）；其他三項分別在處理市場力量與外部性（效率）。

ch2.q: Economists may give conflicting policy advice because they
ch2.qz: 經濟學家為什麼可能給出互相矛盾的政策建議？
o: differ in scientific judgments and in values.
ch2.e: 意見不同的兩個原因：科學判斷不同、價值觀不同。
oz: 他們的科學判斷和價值觀都不同

ch2.q: An economy has 50,000 labor hours. A computer takes 100 hours and a ton of wheat takes 10 hours. Producing 300 computers and 3,500 tons of wheat is
ch2.qz: 一個經濟有 50,000 勞動小時。一台電腦要 100 小時，一噸小麥要 10 小時。生產 300 台電腦和 3,500 噸小麥是

ch2.q: "The government should raise the minimum wage" is a
ch2.qz: 「政府應該調高最低工資」是
o: statement that can be tested with data.
ch2.e: 有 should → 規範 (normative)。
oz: 可以用資料檢驗的敘述

ch2.q: "Lower tax rates encourage more work and more saving" is a
ch2.qz: 「降低稅率會鼓勵人們多工作、多儲蓄」是
ch2.e: 描述因果關係 → 實證 (positive)。

ch2.q: Which of the following is a positive statement?
ch2.qz: 下列哪一個是實證敘述？
o: Prices rise when the government increases the quantity of money.
A tax cut is needed to stimulate the economy.
The government should print less money.
Society ought to require welfare recipients to look for jobs.
ch2.e: (a) 描述關係；其他都是 should／needed／ought。
oz: 政府增加貨幣數量時物價會上漲
社會應該要求領救濟金的人去找工作

ch2.q: Which of the following is a positive statement?
ch2.qz: 下列哪一個是實證敘述？
o: Raising the minimum wage causes unemployment among unskilled workers.
The minimum wage is unfair to small businesses.
The government ought to raise the minimum wage.
oz: 調高最低工資會造成非技術勞工失業
最低工資對小商家不公平
政府應該調高最低工資
勞工應該得到足以生活的工資
ch2.e: 實證敘述是描述「世界是怎樣」，可以用資料檢驗，就算最後被證明是錯的也還是實證敘述。看到 should、ought、fair、deserve 這類價值判斷，就是規範敘述。

ch2.q: Economists try to address their subject with a scientist's objectivity. To do so, they use
ch2.qz: 經濟學家想用科學家的客觀態度研究經濟，所以他們使用
ch2.e: 經濟學家用科學方法：冷靜地建立理論、用資料檢驗（大膽假設，小心求證）。

ch2.q: Why do economists make assumptions?
ch2.qz: 經濟學家為什麼要做假設？
o: To simplify the complex world and make it easier to understand.
Because they cannot collect any data.
To avoid having to make predictions.
To make their models perfectly realistic.
oz: 把複雜的世界簡化，比較容易理解
因為完全收集不到資料
ch2.e: 假設把複雜世界簡化，例如研究貿易時假設只有兩國、兩種商品。

ch2.q: In the circular-flow diagram, households are sellers in
ch2.qz: 在循環流向圖中，家計單位在哪個市場是賣方？
o: the markets for factors of production.
the markets for goods and services.
ch2.e: 家計單位擁有勞動、土地、資本，把它們賣給廠商換所得；在商品市場家計是買方。

ch2.q: In the markets for factors of production, which flows from firms to households?
ch2.qz: 在生產要素市場中，什麼從廠商流向家計單位？
oz: 購買商品和服務的支出
ch2.e: 要素市場：家計提供勞動、土地、資本給廠商；廠商付工資、租金、利潤給家計。錢流和實物流方向相反。

ch2.q: Which of the following is a factor of production?
ch2.qz: 下列哪一個是生產要素？
o: A movie ticket bought by a household
ch2.e: 生產要素：勞動、土地、資本。剪髮、牛奶、電影票都是商品與服務。

ch2.q: A point inside the production possibilities frontier is
ch2.qz: 在生產可能線內部的點是
ch2.e: 線內：做得到，但有資源閒置（失業、工廠空著）→ 沒效率。線上才有效率，線外做不到。

ch2.q: A point outside the production possibilities frontier is
ch2.qz: 在生產可能線外面的點是
o: attainable only if the government prints more money.
not attainable with the economy's current resources and technology.
oz: 政府多印鈔票就做得到
用目前的資源和技術做不到
ch2.e: 線外：資源不夠做不到。印鈔票不會讓 PPF 外移，只有技術進步或資源增加才會。

ch2.q: A production possibilities frontier is bowed outward because
ch2.qz: 生產可能線向外凸，是因為
o: the opportunity cost of a good is constant.
the opportunity cost of a good rises as more of it is produced, since resources are not equally suited to every task.
oz: 商品的機會成本固定不變
生產越多某商品，它的機會成本越高，因為資源不是每種工作都一樣擅長
ch2.e: 向外凸＝機會成本遞增：啤酒廠剩下菁英時再調人去做腳踏車，啤酒產量會大跌。直線才是機會成本固定。

ch2.q: With cloth on the horizontal axis, France's PPF has a slope of 2 and Britain's has a slope of 2/3. Which country has the lower opportunity cost of producing cloth?
ch2.qz: 布在橫軸，法國 PPF 斜率是 2，英國是 2/3。哪一國生產布的機會成本比較低？
ch2.e: 斜率 = 橫軸商品的機會成本。英國 2/3 < 法國 2 → 英國生產布的機會成本較低。

ch2.q: An economy has 50,000 labor hours. A computer takes 100 hours and a ton of wheat takes 10 hours. What is the opportunity cost of one computer?
ch2.qz: 經濟體有 50,000 勞動小時。一台電腦要 100 小時，一噸小麥要 10 小時。一台電腦的機會成本是多少？
ch2.e: 做 1 台電腦的 100 小時可以做 100 ÷ 10 = 10 噸小麥。

ch2.q: In the same economy (50,000 hours; computer 100 h; wheat 10 h), producing 100 computers and 3,000 tons of wheat is
ch2.qz: 同一個經濟體（50,000 小時；電腦 100 小時；小麥 10 小時），生產 100 台電腦和 3,000 噸小麥是

ch2.q: Which of the following is a macroeconomic question?
ch2.qz: 下列哪一個是總體經濟學的問題？
o: How many workers should a firm hire?
How does the growth of the money supply affect the inflation rate?
How do emission rules affect the car industry?
How much should a household save?
oz: 一家廠商應該雇多少人？
貨幣供給成長怎麼影響通膨率？
排放法規怎麼影響汽車業？
一個家庭應該存多少錢？
ch2.e: 總體：通膨、失業、經濟成長等整體現象。家庭、廠商、單一產業的決策是個體。

ch2.q: "Society should require welfare recipients to look for jobs" is a
ch2.qz: 「社會應該要求福利領取者去找工作」是
o: statement that can be tested with data.
oz: 可以用資料驗證的敘述
ch2.e: 「應該」是價值判斷 → 規範（normative）；描述「是什麼」、可以驗證的才是實證。

ch2.q: In the circular-flow diagram, a household that receives $20,000 from its 10 percent ownership of a firm is
ch2.qz: 在循環流向圖中，家計單位因持有某公司 10% 股份收到 $20,000，這是
o: selling goods in the market for goods and services.
buying goods in the market for goods and services.
selling capital in the market for factors of production and receiving profit.
buying labor in the market for factors of production.
oz: 在商品與服務市場賣商品
在商品與服務市場買商品
在生產要素市場提供資本、得到利潤
在生產要素市場買勞動
ch2.e: 資本是生產要素；家計是要素市場的賣方，得到的錢（利潤）流回家計。

ch2.q: Larry can mow 1 lawn or wash 1 car per hour; Moe can mow 1 lawn or wash 2 cars; Curly can mow 2 lawns or wash 1 car. Who has the lowest opportunity cost of mowing a lawn?
ch2.qz: Larry 每小時 1 草或 1 車；Moe 1 草或 2 車；Curly 2 草或 1 車。誰割草的機會成本最低？
ch2.e: 1 片草的機會成本：Larry 1 車、Moe 2 車、Curly 0.5 車 → Curly 最低。

ch2.q: In the Larry–Moe–Curly economy (10 hours each), which allocation is inefficient?
ch2.qz: 在 Larry、Moe、Curly 的經濟（每人 10 小時），哪一種分配沒效率？
o: All three spend half their time on each (20 lawns, 20 cars).
Larry splits his time, Moe only washes, Curly only mows (25, 25).
oz: 每人一半時間（20 草、20 車）
Larry 各半、Moe 只洗車、Curly 只割草（25, 25）
ch2.e: (20, 20) 在 PPF 內：讓 Curly 割 20 片草、Larry 和 Moe 全洗車，可以洗 30 台車。

ch2.q: If only the technology for producing coffee improves, the PPF between coffee (vertical axis) and nuts (horizontal axis)
ch2.qz: 如果只有咖啡（縱軸）的生產技術進步，咖啡與堅果（橫軸）的 PPF 會
o: rotates outward along the coffee axis; the maximum nuts stays the same.
rotates outward along the nuts axis.
oz: 沿咖啡軸往外轉出，堅果最大產量不變
ch2.e: 只有咖啡技術進步，全部做堅果時的產量不變，所以只有咖啡那一端往外。

ch2.q: If the U.S. produced most of its electricity with wind power, it would operate at a point
ch2.qz: 如果美國大部分電力都用風力發電，經濟會落在
ch2.e: 講義 Eye on the Environment：過度依賴風力是沒效率的生產，落在 PPF 內的 Z 點。

ch2.q: "Laws that limit the resale of tickets make audience members worse off on average." About what share of surveyed economists agreed?
ch2.qz: 「限制轉售門票的法律讓觀眾平均變差」大約多少比例的經濟學家同意？
ch2.e: ASK THE EXPERTS：80% 同意、8% 不同意、12% 不確定。

ch3.q: In the U.S., a computer takes 100 hours and a ton of wheat 10 hours. In Japan, a computer takes 125 hours and wheat 25 hours. Which country has a comparative advantage in computers?
ch3.qz: 美國做一台電腦要 100 小時、一噸小麥 10 小時；日本做電腦要 125 小時、小麥 25 小時。哪一國在電腦有比較利益？
ch3.e: 電腦機會成本：美國 100/10 = 10 噸、日本 125/25 = 5 噸 → 日本較低。

ch3.q: In the same example (U.S.: computer 100 h, wheat 10 h; Japan: computer 125 h, wheat 25 h), which statement is correct?
ch3.qz: 同一個例子（美國：電腦 100 小時、小麥 10 小時；日本：電腦 125 小時、小麥 25 小時），哪個敘述正確？
o: Japan has an absolute advantage in both goods.
The U.S. has an absolute advantage in both goods.
The U.S. has a comparative advantage in both goods.
ch3.e: 美國兩樣都用比較少小時 → 兩樣都有絕對優勢，但比較優勢只會有一樣。
oz: 日本兩種商品都有絕對利益
美國兩種商品都有絕對利益
美國兩種商品都有比較利益
兩國都無法從貿易得利

ch3.q: Which statement is true?
ch3.qz: 哪個敘述正確？
o: Certain talented people have a comparative advantage in everything.
If a trade is good for one person, it cannot be good for the other.
Two countries can gain from trade even if one has an absolute advantage in all goods.
If trade is good for a country, it must be good for everyone in the country.
ch3.e: 貿易利得來自比較優勢，不需要絕對優勢。
oz: 某些有才華的人在所有事情上都有比較利益
如果交易對一個人好，就不可能對另一個人也好
即使一國在所有商品都有絕對利益，兩國仍能從貿易得利
如果貿易對一國有利，就一定對該國每個人都有利

ch3.q: For trade to benefit both parties, the price of a good (in terms of the other good) must be
ch3.qz: 要讓雙方都從貿易得利，一種商品的價格（用另一種商品表示）必須
o: between the two parties' opportunity costs.
ch3.e: 交易價格要介於兩方機會成本之間。
oz: 介於雙方的機會成本之間

ch3.q: Comparative advantage is based on
ch3.qz: 比較利益是根據什麼決定的？
ch3.e: 比較優勢 = 機會成本較低。

ch3.q: A producer has an absolute advantage in a good if it
ch3.qz: 生產者在一項商品有絕對利益，是指它
o: can produce it using fewer inputs.
ch3.e: 絕對優勢 = 用較少投入。
oz: 用比較少的投入就能生產

ch3.q: The gains from trade arise from
ch3.qz: 貿易的好處來自
ch3.e: 貿易利得來自比較優勢。

ch3.q: A German worker takes 400 hours to make a car and 2 hours to make a case of wine. A French worker takes 600 hours for a car and X hours for wine. Germany will export cars if
ch3.qz: 德國工人做一台車要 400 小時、一箱酒要 2 小時；法國工人做一台車要 600 小時、一箱酒要 X 小時。在什麼條件下德國會出口汽車？
ch3.e: 德國車機會成本 200 箱酒；法國 600/X。德國較低 → 200 < 600/X → X < 3。

ch3.q: A person has a comparative advantage in producing a good when

ch5.e: 完全有彈性 = 水平；完全無彈性 = 垂直。越平越有彈性。

ch5.q: Demand is P = 100 − Q. At a price of $75, demand is
ch5.qz: 需求是 P = 100 − Q。價格 $75 時，需求是

inelastic, so raising the price would raise total revenue.
unit elastic, so total revenue is at its maximum.
oz: 富有彈性，降價會讓總收益增加
缺乏彈性，漲價會讓總收益增加
單一彈性，總收益在最大值

ch5.q: Along the linear demand curve P = 100 − Q, total revenue is largest when the price is
ch5.qz: 在直線需求線 P = 100 − Q 上，價格多少時總收益最大？
ch5.e: 總收益在中點（單一彈性）最大：P = 50、Q = 50、TR = 2,500。

ch5.q: For which good is the price elasticity of demand likely to be largest?
ch5.qz: 哪一項商品的需求價格彈性最可能最大？
ch5.e: 商品定義越窄、替代品越多，彈性越大：星巴克拿鐵 > 所有飲料；胰島素和水是必需品，彈性很小。

ch5.qz: 汽油的需求
o: more elastic in the short run than in the long run.
equally elastic in the short run and the long run.
perfectly inelastic in the long run.
more elastic in the long run than in the short run.
ch5.e: 時間越長越有彈性：長期可以換小車、搬近一點、改搭大眾運輸。

ch5.q: When income rises 10%, the quantity demanded of good X rises 25%. Good X is

ch5.e: 所得彈性 = 25 / 10 = 2.5：大於 0 是正常財，大於 1 是奢侈品。

ch5.q: If the cross-price elasticity of demand between two goods is positive, the goods are
ch5.qz: 如果兩個商品的交叉價格彈性是正的，它們是
ch5.e: 交叉彈性 > 0：A 漲價，B 多買 → 替代品；< 0 是互補品。

ch5.q: A new hybrid wheat raises wheat output by 20%. Because the demand for wheat is inelastic, farmers' total revenue will
ch5.qz: 新品種小麥讓產量增加 20%。因為小麥需求缺乏彈性，農民的總收益會
o: rise, because they sell more wheat.
fall, because the price falls by a larger percentage than quantity rises.
oz: 上升，因為賣出更多小麥
下降，因為價格跌的 % 比數量增加的 % 大
ch5.e: 供給右移 + 需求缺乏彈性 → 價格大跌、數量小增 → 總收益下降（$300 → $220）：農業好消息是農民的壞消息。

ch5.q: Drug interdiction reduces the supply of illegal drugs. Because the demand for drugs is inelastic, interdiction tends to
ch5.qz: 查緝毒品讓毒品供給減少。因為毒品需求缺乏彈性，查緝通常會
o: reduce total spending on drugs and crime.
raise total spending on drugs and may increase drug-related crime.
oz: 讓毒品總支出和犯罪都減少
讓毒品總支出增加，可能使與毒品相關的犯罪增加
ch5.e: 供給左移 + 需求缺乏彈性 → 價格大漲、總支出增加 → 為了買毒的犯罪增加。反毒教育讓需求左移，才會讓犯罪減少。

ch5.q: Which good is likely to have the most inelastic supply?
ch5.qz: 哪一項商品的供給最可能最缺乏彈性？
ch5.e: 賣方越難調整產量，供給彈性越小。海景地幾乎不能增加 → 供給很缺乏彈性；需求增加時價格大漲。

o: Vacationers' demand is more elastic than business travelers'.
Both demands have the same elasticity.
oz: 商務旅客需求富有彈性
度假旅客需求比商務旅客更有彈性
度假旅客需求完全無彈性
ch5.e: 商務 0.23、度假 1.29。度假旅客替代選擇多。

ch5.q: A price change reduces quantity demanded by 30 percent while total revenue rises by 15 percent. Demand is
ch5.qz: 價格變動使需求量減少 30%，總收益卻增加 15%。需求是

ch5.q: Coffee and donuts are complements, both with inelastic demand. A hurricane destroys half the coffee bean crop. Total spending on cups of coffee will

ch5.e: 供給減少 → 價格上漲；需求缺乏彈性 → 總支出上升。（甜甜圈需求左移，支出下降。）

ch5.q: Drug interdiction reduces the supply of illegal drugs. Because drug demand is inelastic, drug-related crime tends to
ch5.qz: 查緝減少毒品供給。因為毒品需求缺乏彈性，毒品相關犯罪會

rise, because total spending on drugs rises.
oz: 增加，因為毒品總支出上升
ch5.e: P 漲的比例大於 Q 降的比例 → 吸毒者總支出增加 → 犯罪增加。

ch5.q: Population growth doubles demand for both beachfront property (inelastic supply) and new cars (elastic supply). Which is true?
ch5.qz: 人口成長使海濱房地產（供給缺乏彈性）和新車（供給有彈性）的需求都加倍。哪個正確？
o: The price of new cars rises more.
The price of beachfront property rises more, and the quantity of new cars rises more.
Quantities change by the same amount.
oz: 海濱房地產價格漲比較多，新車數量增加比較多
ch5.e: 供給越缺乏彈性，需求增加越反映在價格上。

ch5.q: When the price of a burger falls, the demand for pizza decreases. The cross-price elasticity of demand between pizza and burgers is

ch5.e: S 右移 → 價格大跌、數量小增 → TR 下降（講義 $300 → $220）。

ch5.q: OPEC kept oil prices high in the 1970s but not over the long run, mainly because

the government imposed a price ceiling.
oz: 石油需求變成完全無彈性
長期的供給和需求比較有彈性
ch5.e: 長期消費者換省油車、非 OPEC 國家增產（頁岩油），減產只讓價格小漲。

ch6.q: A price ceiling set below the equilibrium price causes

ch6.e: 上限低於均衡 → binding → 短缺。

ch6.q: A price ceiling set above the equilibrium price
ch6.qz: 訂在均衡價格之上的價格上限
o: is not binding and has no effect.
ch6.e: 上限在上面 → 不具約束力。

ch6.q: A minimum wage set above the equilibrium wage causes
ch6.qz: 最低工資訂在均衡工資之上會造成
ch6.e: 下限高於均衡 → 勞動過剩 = 失業。

ch6.q: A binding price ceiling is raised but stays below the equilibrium price. The shortage will
ch6.qz: 有約束力的價格上限被調高，但仍低於均衡價格。短缺會
ch6.e: 上限越接近均衡價格，需求量減少、供給量增加，兩者差距（短缺）變小。只有調到均衡以上才會完全消失。

ch6.q: In a hotel market, equilibrium is P = $100 and Q = 100 rooms. With a price ceiling of $90, quantity demanded is 120 and quantity supplied is 90. The result is
ch6.qz: 飯店市場的均衡是 P = $100、Q = 100 間。價格上限 $90 時，需求量 120、供給量 90。結果是
o: no effect, because the ceiling is not binding.
oz: 沒有影響，因為上限不具約束力
ch6.e: 上限 $90 低於均衡 → 有約束力 → 短缺 = 120 − 90 = 30。

ch6.q: In the same hotel market (equilibrium P = $100), a price floor of $120 gives quantity demanded 60 and quantity supplied 120. The result is
ch6.qz: 同一個飯店市場（均衡 P = $100），價格下限 $120 時需求量 60、供給量 120。結果是
o: no effect, because the floor is not binding.
oz: 沒有影響，因為下限不具約束力
ch6.e: 下限 $120 高於均衡 → 有約束力 → 過剩 = 120 − 60 = 60。

ch6.q: Supply is QS = 2P and demand is QD = 300 − P. What are the equilibrium price and quantity?
ch6.qz: 供給 QS = 2P，需求 QD = 300 − P。均衡價格和數量是多少？

ch6.qz: 供給 QS = 2P，需求 QD = 300 − P。對賣方課每單位 $30 的稅。買方付多少、賣方拿多少？
o: Buyers pay $130, sellers receive $100, and Q = 170
Buyers pay $110, sellers receive $80, and Q = 190
Buyers pay $100, sellers receive $70, and Q = 200
Buyers pay $120, sellers receive $90, and Q = 180
ch6.e: 賣方實拿 PS = PB − 30：2(PB − 30) = 300 − PB → PB = 120、PS = 90、Q = 180。原均衡 P = 100：買方多付 20，賣方少拿 10。

ch6.q: A pizza sells for $10 and 500 are sold. After a $1.50 tax per pizza, buyers pay $11.00 and sellers receive $9.50. How is the tax burden shared?
ch6.qz: 披薩原價 $10、賣 500 個。每個課 $1.50 的稅後，買方付 $11.00、賣方拿 $9.50。稅的負擔怎麼分？
o: Buyers bear $1.00 and sellers bear $0.50 per pizza.
oz: 買方每個負擔 $1.00，賣方負擔 $0.50

ch6.q: The burden of a tax falls more heavily on
ch6.qz: 稅的負擔會比較多落在
o: the side of the market that is less elastic.
the side of the market that is more elastic.
whichever side the law says must pay the tax.
oz: 市場上彈性比較小的那一方
市場上彈性比較大的那一方
法律規定要繳稅的那一方
ch6.e: 租稅歸宿跟法律規定誰繳無關；彈性小的一方比較難離開市場，負擔較多。

ch6.q: The 1990 U.S. luxury tax on yachts was meant to tax the rich. Who actually bore most of it?
ch6.qz: 1990 年美國對遊艇課的奢侈稅是想讓有錢人繳稅。實際上誰負擔最多？
o: The firms and workers who build yachts, because yacht demand was elastic and supply inelastic
Rich buyers, because they can afford it
oz: 造遊艇的廠商和工人，因為遊艇需求有彈性、供給缺乏彈性
有錢的買方，因為他們付得起
ch6.e: 有錢人可以改買別的（需求有彈性），造船廠和工人很難轉行（供給缺乏彈性）→ 負擔落在供給方。1993 年大部分廢除。

ch6.q: The law splits the payroll (FICA) tax equally between employers and workers. Who actually bears most of it?
ch6.qz: 法律規定薪資稅（FICA）由雇主和勞工各付一半。實際上誰負擔最多？
o: Workers, because labor supply is less elastic than labor demand
They each bear exactly half, as the law says
Employers, because they write the checks
oz: 勞工，因為勞動供給比勞動需求缺乏彈性
雙方各負擔一半，跟法律規定的一樣
ch6.e: 負擔看彈性不看法律：勞動供給較缺乏彈性 → 勞工負擔大部分。

ch6.q: Under a binding price ceiling, which way of rationing the good is likely to appear?
ch6.qz: 有約束力的價格上限下，可能出現哪種分配商品的方式？
o: Sellers advertising heavily to attract buyers
Long lines, discrimination by sellers and bribes
oz: 賣方大做廣告吸引買方
排隊、賣方依偏好歧視、賄賂
ch6.e: 短缺時價格不能分配，只好排隊、看賣方喜歡誰、賄賂，這些方法不公平也沒效率。

ch6.q: Why is the shortage caused by rent control larger in the long run than in the short run?
ch6.qz: 為什麼租金管制造成的短缺，長期比短期更大？
o: Supply and demand for housing are more elastic in the long run.
Supply and demand are more inelastic in the long run.
Landlords build more apartments over time.
oz: 長期的住房供給和需求更有彈性
長期的供需更缺乏彈性
房東會隨時間蓋更多公寓
ch6.e: 短期供需缺乏彈性 → 短缺小；長期房東不蓋新房、不維修，更多人想搬進城市 → 短缺變大。

ch6.q: Economists generally prefer which way of helping the poor over rent control?
ch6.qz: 經濟學家通常認為，比起租金管制，用哪種方式幫助窮人比較好？
o: Rent subsidies or wage subsidies such as the EITC
oz: 租金補貼或薪資補貼（例如 EITC）
ch6.e: 價格管制讓價格無法平衡供需；租金補貼、薪資補貼（EITC）幫窮人又不造成短缺。

ch6.qz: 均衡租金 $800 時設 $500 的租金上限。和短期相比，長期的短缺
o: smaller, because supply and demand are less elastic.
larger, because supply and demand are more elastic.
oz: 比較小，因為供需比較沒彈性
比較大，因為供需比較有彈性
ch6.e: 長期房東不蓋不修、更多人想租 → 短缺變大（講義 250/400 → 150/450）。

ch6.q: Frisbee market: equilibrium P = $8, Q = 6 million. A price floor of $10 is imposed. Quantity sold is

ch6.e: $10 時需求量 200 萬、供給量 1,200 萬 → 只賣得掉 200 萬。

ch6.qz: 每片 $1.50 的稅使均衡從 $10、500 片變成買方付 $11、賣方拿 $9.50。稅負是

ch6.q: A tax on buyers shifts the
ch6.qz: 對買方課稅會讓

demand curve up by the amount of the tax.
supply curve up by the amount of the tax.
supply curve down by the amount of the tax.
ch6.e: 買方要付稅，願付的市場價格就少了稅額 → D 往下移。

ch6.q: In 1990 the U.S. taxed yachts. Because yacht demand is elastic and supply is inelastic in the short run, the tax burden fell mostly on
ch6.qz: 1990 年美國對遊艇課奢侈稅。因為遊艇需求有彈性、短期供給缺乏彈性，稅負主要落在
ch6.e: 稅負落在比較沒彈性的那一方（賣方）。奢侈稅大部分在 1993 年廢除。

ch6.q: In 2011 the workers' share of the payroll tax fell from 6.2% to 4.2%. If labor supply and labor demand both have positive elasticity, workers' take-home pay rises by
ch6.qz: 2011 年勞工負擔的工資稅從 6.2% 降到 4.2%。若勞動供給和需求彈性都大於 0，勞工實拿薪水會增加
ch6.e: 減稅好處由勞工和雇主分享，勞工拿到的少於 2%。

ch6.q: Supply is Qs = 2P and demand is Qd = 300 − P. A price ceiling of $90 causes a
ch6.qz: 供給 Qs = 2P、需求 Qd = 300 − P。價格上限 $90 會造成

ch7.q: Consumer surplus is
ch7.qz: 消費者剩餘是
o: the price minus the seller's cost.
the amount a buyer is willing to pay minus the price actually paid.
the number of extra buyers in a market.
ch7.e: CS = WTP − P。
oz: 買方的願付價格減掉實際付的價格
市場中多出來的買方人數

ch7.q: Producer surplus is
ch7.qz: 生產者剩餘是
o: the price received minus the seller's cost.
the number of extra sellers in a market.
ch7.e: PS = P − cost。
oz: 收到的價格減掉賣方成本
市場中多出來的賣方人數

ch7.q: On a supply-and-demand graph, consumer surplus is the area
ch7.qz: 在供需圖上，消費者剩餘是哪一塊面積？

below the demand curve and above the price.
between the two curves beyond equilibrium.
ch7.e: 需求線以下、價格以上。

ch7.qz: 買方的願付價格是
o: the price the buyer actually pays.
the average price in the market.
the maximum amount the buyer will pay for a good.
the seller's cost of producing the good.

ch7.qz: 四個買方對 iPod 的願付價格：Flea $300、Anthony $250、Chad $175、John $125。價格 $260 時，消費者剩餘是

ch7.e: CS = 需求線以下、價格以上的三角形 = ½ × 15 × (60 − 30) = 225。

buyers who stay in the market pay more, and some buyers leave the market.

oz: 賣方必須放棄的一切，包含自己時間的機會成本
